newsitem.title: BELGIUM: German, French politicians to set OLO agenda.
newsitem.headline: German, French politicians to set OLO agenda.

text.p: Statements by German and French politicians on EMU will set the entire agenda for Belgian linear bonds from now on, traders said on Tuesday.
"We'll go up and down depending on comments by politicians from France and Germany, the others don't count," said Dirk Laenen at CERA Bank.
Laenen said he expected OLO prices to remain in a tight range in the weeks ahead, barring a failure of the EU summit in Amsterdam next week.
"But I think it's too early for that, (EU government leaders) will try and hammer out a compromise," he said.
OLO activity was modest and focusing on 10-year paper.

The prospect of the OLO exchange auction later on Tuesday temporarily pushed the 10-year OLO/Bund yield spread up by one basis point to 10 but Laenen said it was now at the top of the range and would narrow again after the auction.
The Treasury is offering OLO lines 27 (4.00 pct, Jan 2000), 10 (8.75 pct, June 2002), 20 (7.75 pct, Oct 2004) and 26 (6.25 pct March 2007) against OLO 8 (9.25 pct, Aug 1997) and 4 (9.25 pct, Jan 98).
Dealers expected the Treasury to continue its policy of relatively low allocation, favouring T-bill auctions instead.
T-bill yields were steady ahead of the weekly auction. The franc also held up well after having suffered some spill-over pressure from the French franc on Monday.
